# Use Case Fit

Dimension covering where each tool excels and when to choose one over the other.
See [citations.md](../citations.md) for full source details.

## Where Notion Excels

### Team Collaboration and Project Management

Notion is built for teams. It offers real-time co-editing with unlimited
participants [7], five permission levels [6], member/guest/group role management
[13], and database automations for workflow management [19]. The productive.io
comparison recommends Notion for "team collaboration, integrated task management,
calendar sync, complex relational data with AI" [17].

### Structured Data and Databases

Notion databases support 8 view types (Table, Board, Timeline, Calendar, List,
Gallery, Chart, Form) and 19+ property types with Relations, Rollups, and
Formulas [16]. This makes Notion function as a lightweight project management
tool, CRM, or content calendar without external software.

### All-in-One Workspace

Notion bundles notes, wikis, databases, project management, web publishing,
calendar, email, and AI into a single platform [1]. For teams wanting to
consolidate tools, this reduces context-switching.

### Web Publishing

Notion Sites allow publishing pages directly to the web with auto-updates,
SEO controls, and custom domains [12]. No separate hosting or build step
required.

## Where Obsidian Excels

### Personal Knowledge Management (PKM)

Obsidian's knowledge graph, bi-directional linking, and Canvas are designed
for building a personal knowledge base [17]. The graph view visualizes
connections between notes in ways Notion cannot replicate natively.

### Privacy and Data Ownership

All data stays on the user's local filesystem as plain markdown files [17].
No cloud dependency, no vendor access to content, no terms-of-service
governing stored data.

### Offline-First Workflows

Every feature works without internet connectivity. Notion's offline mode is
opt-in, per-page, limited to 50 database rows, and per-device [9]. Obsidian
is fully offline by default.

### Deep Customization

Obsidian's community plugin ecosystem (reported 2,600+ plugins, unverified)
enables capabilities from Kanban boards to AI integrations to Dataview queries.
The open plugin API allows building custom integrations without vendor
gatekeeping.

### Cost

Obsidian is free for personal use. Core features require no subscription.
Sync ($8/month equivalent) and Publish ($8/month per site) are optional
paid add-ons [17]. Notion's free tier has meaningful restrictions (5MB uploads,
7-day history, 10 guests, limited blocks for 2+ members) [3].

## Decision Framework

| Factor | Choose Notion | Choose Obsidian |
|--------|--------------|-----------------|
| Team size | 2+ people collaborating | Solo or minimal sharing |
| Data sensitivity | Acceptable in vendor cloud | Must stay local |
| Internet access | Reliably available | Unreliable or restricted |
| Primary use | Project management, wikis, databases | Research, writing, PKM |
| Structured data | Relational databases needed | Flat notes with frontmatter sufficient |
| Budget | Free tier adequate for solo; team = $10-24/member/month [3] | Free for personal; $8/month for sync |
| Extensibility | Built-in features + API | Community plugins |
| Data portability | Export is lossy [5] | Files are the source format |

## Hybrid Usage

Multiple comparison sources note that power users run both tools for different
purposes — Notion for team coordination, Obsidian for personal thinking.
The productive.io comparison implicitly supports this: Obsidian's sync
limitation pushes users toward Notion for cross-device team needs, while
Notion's offline limitations push heavy offline users toward Obsidian [17].

## Gaps and Limitations

- Use case recommendations are primarily from productive.io [17], a single
  third-party source with potential bias (the article promotes their own
  product as an alternative)
- No user survey data or market research on actual usage patterns
- Notion's scaling characteristics for large teams (100+ members) are not
  documented in fetched sources
- Obsidian's commercial licensing requirements for business use were mentioned
  but not detailed from official sources
